title: Faith never without some apprehension; apprehension precedes faith but is not faith
source_text: XXVI. Caeterum non negant, imo expresse docent fidem non esse sine apprehensione aliqua, rudi saltem & confusa, eorum quae creduntur: ac proinde in eo qui credit haec duo reperiri, 1. apprehensionem, 2. judicium sive assensum, licet apprehensio illa proprie non sit fides, sed aliquid fidem praecedens.
pass_a_gloss: Yet they do not deny, indeed they expressly teach, that faith is not without some apprehension, at least rude and confused, of the things that are believed; and therefore in the one who believes these two are found: first apprehension, second judgment or assent, although that apprehension is not properly faith, but something preceding faith.
pass_b_english: Rome still grants that faith never lacks some apprehension, at least rude and confused, of what is believed.
In the believer there are two: apprehension and judgment or assent; apprehension properly is not faith but something that precedes it.

choices.why: Apprehension required but not identical with faith.
